name: What is the difference between an open floor plan and a wall removal?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between an open floor plan conversion and simply removing one wall?
mainEntity.text: What is the difference between an open floor plan conversion and simply removing one wall?

acceptedAnswer.text: A single wall removal can create a larger opening, but it does not automatically create a good open floor plan. True open-concept remodeling usually addresses circulation, furniture placement, sight lines, storage, lighting, and how the kitchen, dining, and living areas work together. It may also require a beam, hidden support posts, new electrical layout, HVAC balancing, and seamless floor patching. This is why some projects feel “opened up” but still look unfinished or awkward. Homeowners comparing bids should look for scope language that includes both structure and design integration, not just demolition. The best results come from planning the new space as a whole instead of treating the wall as the only problem to solve.
acceptedAnswer.description: Removing one wall is only one part of an open-floor-plan conversion. A true conversion often also includes structural support, lighting changes, flooring transitions, HVAC adjustments, and layout redesign so the new space functions well.
